name: @opennous/mcp

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Report who this API key acts AS: the workspace, the person, their SCOPE (admin sees the whole workspace; member sees only their own book plus the shared graph), their GTM ROLE(S) (e.g. AE, SDR, founder — a person can hold several), the key's capability (read/write vs read-only), and the budget left (plan, ops left, credits left; unlimited when the plan has no cap). Call it to confirm the plugin is wired to the right workspace and identity, and to scope role-specific work to the right person — a member gets their own view, an admin the whole team's.

tools.name: find

search.description: people: name, email, company or LinkedIn contains. accounts: name, domain or email contains. Not for deals.

stage.description: Canonical stage, e.g. demo, negotiation, closed_won. people/accounts/deals.

last_activity_before.description: Gone quiet: no activity in this long, e.g. '30d', '12h' (includes never active). people/accounts.

last_activity_after.description: Active within this long, e.g. '7d'. people/accounts.

account.description: One account: domain, entity UUID, email or name. people/deals.

include_all.description: people: everyone incl. cold leads (fewer filters). accounts: skip the list window (by default: an open or won deal, a recent loss, or recent activity).

status.description: deals: open | won | lost. people: record status, e.g. active.

closing_within_days.description: Open deals whose close date is between today and N days out. deals.

min_amount.description: Amount at least this (deals without an amount drop out). deals.

implied.description: true = only implied deals, false = only CRM deals. deals.

source.description: Where the person came from, e.g. hubspot, linkedin, gmail, manual. people.

filters.description: Only the filters the chosen kind supports (see the description).

sort.description: Default last_activity (newest first). Each kind has its own set (see the description).

limit.description: Page size (default 50 for accounts/deals, 100 for people).

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: Get engineered context for a specific task about a person, a company or a DEAL. Pass their email (or entity id, or a deal id from find { kind: 'deals' }) and the intent. A deal id leads with the DEAL itself (stage, amount, close date, owner, health, the people on it, the objections / competitors / budget / timeline filed to it), then its account's context. Returns a focused, ranked context block: the facts that matter for that task — each with a confidence and a freshness — the durable FACTS we've learned about them (their atomic memory: budget, authority, pain, stack, plans), the recent timeline, the buying-group stakeholders, open predictions, and the account's ICP fit score (0-100 + why). Call this before drafting outreach, preparing for a meeting, or making any decision about a person. A fact's freshness tells you whether to trust it: 'fresh' act on it, 'suspect'/'expired' verify first.

focus.description: Who or what to look up — an email, a LinkedIn URL, a domain, an entity UUID, a name, or a DEAL id: a CRM deal UUID, or `implied:<account_id>` for an account with no CRM deal (both as find { kind: 'deals' } prints them). A name may match several people; you'll get candidates to choose from.

intent.description: What you are about to do — shapes which context surfaces (default: account_review)

budget_tokens.description: Approximate token budget for the context block

tools.name: query
tools.description:
Retrieve and summarise activity across many people. Three powers:
  1. return:'entities' groups results by person/company (one row per entity, ranked by most-recent matching activity). Use for 'hottest leads', 'who replied this week', 'who's in the negotiation stage'.
  2. `without` subtracts entities — 'sent in 5d MINUS replied in 5d' = 'no-reply leads'. 'activity in 30d MINUS activity in 5d' = 'cooled leads'.
  3. rollups.by_value appears when scope.kind='state' — counts entities by current value (use scope.property='stage' for funnel reports).
  4. Scheduled meetings/calls are events with property 'interaction.meeting_scheduled' and a future-dated `when`. For 'what's booked today/this week', set property:'interaction.meeting_scheduled' with from/to bounding the day or week (since_days only looks backward and can't reach them), and order:'asc' to list soonest-first. Meeting rows render the absolute date and time.
  5. scope.facts:true + question searches the FACTS corpus (durable atomic facts about accounts) instead of activity — cross-account semantic fact search like 'which accounts want off Clay' or 'who is hiring'. return:'entities' gives the single best-matching fact per account. (A single account's facts already come back inline with get_account.) READ THE ICP ITSELF with scope:{foundation:'icp'} — the buyer definition and the scoring rules, not another number derived from them. Do that before triaging a list or arguing with a score, so the judgement is one you can explain.

property.description: property prefix — 'interaction.email' covers email_sent and email_replied; 'interaction.meeting_scheduled' for booked meetings

since_days.description: only activity within the last N days (backward only)

from.description: ISO timestamp — only activity at/after this (absolute lower bound; use for date windows like 'today')

to.description: ISO timestamp — only activity at/before this (absolute upper bound). Combine from+to for a window; future-dated for upcoming meetings

order.description: observed_at order (default desc, newest first). Use 'asc' for an upcoming-meeting schedule (soonest first)

facts.description: search the FACTS corpus (durable atomic facts about accounts) instead of activity. Needs `question` — a cross-account semantic fact search, e.g. 'which accounts want off Clay'. return:'entities' = the best matching fact per account.

reporting.description: Return the distilled REPORTING for a seat instead of activity: 'role' = the insights routed to a GTM role (deal-blockers/objections with account counts + relevant themes, reframed for that seat); 'company' = the whole-company founder lens. Routed server-side by the caller's role — a member only ever gets their own seat, an admin/founder can ask for 'company' or any role.

role.description: With reporting:'role', which seat to report for — account_executive | sdr | sales | customer_success | engineer | marketing | revops | founder. Defaults to the caller's own role(s) from whoami.

attention.description: Return the daily WORKLIST instead of activity: the engine-curated Studio surface — upcoming meetings, the follow-ups you owe, and the accounts to focus on (open attention flags) — scoped to the caller (a member sees only their owned book; an admin/founder sees the whole workspace). Powers the morning read.

foundation.description: Return a FOUNDATION document as written instead of activity: 'icp' = the ICP itself, the buyer definition and the scoring rules, not another number derived from them. Read this before triaging a list, planning an account, or arguing with a score, so the judgement is one you can explain.

without.description: Subtract entities matching this scope from the result — same shape as scope. Enables 'sent but no reply', 'cooled in last N days'.

return.description: observations (default) = one row per observation. entities = one row per entity, ranked by most-recent matching activity.

question.description: What you want to learn — echoed back; enables semantic ranking

tools.name: attention
tools.description: What needs attention NOW, workspace-wide and ranked: accounts going dark, key facts that have decayed, upcoming meetings, open commitments, hot intent, and flags. Each item names the account, what happened, a suggested action and where it came from. Use it for 'what should I do today', 'who's gone quiet', 'what did I promise'. Open commitments carry a task id: when the user says one is done, close it with `tasks` (action 'done') so it leaves every worklist. A member key sees its own book.

tools.name: tasks
tools.description: The TASK LIST: the commitments and next steps Nous extracted from calls, meetings and emails, plus tasks people added by hand. One tool to read them and to close them. action 'list' (default) returns tasks with a task id, the account, who owes it, the due date and where it came from. action 'done' closes tasks by id; 'reopen' puts them back. Use 'done' the moment the user says a task is finished ("I sent the deck", "mark those done"), or when you can see it was done: a closed task leaves the Tasks page, attention and every report. Never write a note to say a task is done; close it here. Ids come from this tool's list or from attention. To find one task, list with `focus` set to the account.

ids.description: For done/reopen: task ids ('<entity_id>:action_item.…'), up to 100.

reason.description: For done: what made it done, in a few words, e.g. 'deck sent 10 Oct'. Shown on the task.

owner.description: For list: whose tasks. me (default) = our side; prospect = what they owe us.

focus.description: For list: one account or person, by entity UUID or email.

due.description: For list: only tasks due today or within 7 days. Default all.

tools.name: rules
tools.description: The user's RULES for their own deals, said once. Add one the moment the user states how their deals must go ("every meeting ends with a dated next step within 48 hours", "I reply to buyers within a day", "lead with ROI for CFOs"). If it matches a check, pass `check` (and its number) and the engine holds them to it in the background: a broken rule raises the account in attention and opens a task, and both clear once it is met. Checks: next_step_after_meeting (hours), reply_to_buyer_email (hours), stage_without_meeting (days); action 'checks' says what each verifies. A rule that matches none is guidance: pass no check, tell the user it is guidance, and apply it yourself. action 'list' (default) shows their rules with ids; 'pause', 'resume', 'remove' take `id`. Rules are personal (a member key).

action.description: list (default), add, pause, resume, remove, or checks.

statement.description: For add: the rule in the user's words.

check.description: For add: the check this rule maps onto. Omit for guidance.

hours.description: For add: the window in hours (next_step_after_meeting, reply_to_buyer_email).

days.description: For add: the window in days (stage_without_meeting).

weight.description: For add: how hard a broken rule pushes the account up. Default normal.

id.description: For pause/resume/remove: the rule id from list.

tools.name: get_insights
tools.description: Read the INSIGHTS BOARD: what customers said about OUR business, each insight placed under the team that has to act (lane: product | sales | success | market) and the kind of work (subtype: bug, friction, feature, objection, pricing, pitch, setup, training, partners, buyers), tagged with the concrete thing it is about, and tied to the account that said it, with the quote and speaker. Filter by lane, subtype, one account (`focus`), or a date. Use for 'what objections are we hearing', 'which bugs came up this month', 'what did Acme ask for'. The labels follow the workspace (a service business sees Delivery / Missed results). To WRITE an insight use record_insight.

subtype.description: The kind of work. Must belong to `lane` when both are given.

focus.description: One account: entity UUID, email, domain, or LinkedIn URL (not a bare name).

since.description: Only insights on or after this ISO date, e.g. 2026-09-01.

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Keep a NOTE or document on a person or company: a short note, a meeting brief, meeting notes, a pre-meeting prep, research, or a transcript. It is stored on the account and found later by the account reads. This is for artifacts you keep, not interactions: for 'an email was sent' or 'a meeting happened' use record; for a finished brief/plan/report you want in Pages use save_page. `focus` must be an entity UUID, email, LinkedIn URL or domain (a domain files on the company); an unknown email or domain creates the person/company.

focus.description: Who it is about: entity UUID, email, LinkedIn URL, or domain. Not a bare name.

title.description: A short name, e.g. 'Pre-meeting brief: renewal'.

date.description: The relevant date (e.g. the meeting date), ISO. Defaults to now.

tools.name: enrich
tools.description: ENRICH one person, or one company, on the workspace's OWN providers (Apollo / Findymail / Prospeo, its keys; Nous adds no data of its own). A person: title, email, LinkedIn, company, phone, location. A company (`account`: domain or account id): industry, size, location, keywords, description, tech stack, which every person there inherits, so it fills the FIT part of their scores. Re-scores on the live ICP. Anything enriched in the last 90 days comes back from what we already hold, nothing spent; pass force:true to buy it again. Spends the workspace's enrichment credits: enrich what you are about to work, not a whole list.

person.description: The person: entity UUID, email, or LinkedIn URL (not a name; find { kind: 'people', search } first).

account.description: Instead of a person, a company: its domain (acme.com) or account entity id.

force.description: Re-enrich even inside the 90-day reuse window. Spends a credit.

tools.name: score
tools.description: Score a lead against our live ICP model and intent axis, and write the judgment into the graph so every other agent reads the same number. This is for scoring a list the user built ELSEWHERE (a Google Sheet, a Clay column, a CRM export): the list stays where it is, Nous returns the score. Give an email, domain, LinkedIn URL, or entity UUID (or up to 100 at once via `identifiers`). Returns ICP fit 0-100 + tier (tier_1/2/3/not_icp, which drives the play), decaying intent 0-100 + band, AND the LAYERED read: layers {fit,pain,intent,ability} with a `missing` worklist (what's still unknown — unknown is never 0) and a suggested `play`. It reads the live score (staking one on demand for a known-but-unscored account); the score keeps evolving afterwards. COLD LEAD not in Nous? Pass `attributes` (title, company, keywords/headline) and it's scored INLINE against the model — Fit/Pain resolve from what you have, nothing is written. For a whole EXTERNAL list, pass `leads` (up to 1000 attribute objects) — all scored inline in one call, model loaded once, nothing written — so you can triage a big list before deciding what to bring in. Only a bare identifier with no attributes and no graph record comes back `unknown_identifier`. BRING YOUR OWN SCORER: when the workspace scores with its own system (whoami / GET /v2/icp/scorer says 'external'; the API plan does by default), pass `scorer` (your model's name) and `scores` [{identifier, score 0-100, tier?, reason?}] to WRITE your scores onto the record instead. They become the fit every other agent reads, and Nous grades them against won/lost.

identifier.description: One lead — an email, domain, LinkedIn URL, or entity UUID.

identifiers.description: A batch of graph leads (max 100 per call; loop for a larger list).

attributes.description: For a COLD lead NOT in Nous: its attributes from LinkedIn/a list — { job_title, seniority, company_type, industry, employee_count, keywords or headline, location }. Scored inline against the model; nothing is written. Use when the identifier isn't in the graph yet, or pass on its own with no identifier.

leads.description: An EXTERNAL cold list scored inline in one call (up to 1000): each item is an attributes object { job_title, company_type, keywords|headline, ... }, optionally with a `ref` echoed back. Nothing is written to the graph. Use to triage a big list before deciding which accounts to bring in.

intent.description: Optional hint about why you're scoring. Currently ignored; it does not change the score.

scorer.description: With `scores`: the name of YOUR scoring model, e.g. 'acme-v3' (letters, digits, . _ - /). Stamped on each score.

identifier.description: email, domain, LinkedIn URL, or entity UUID of an account already in Nous

tier.description: your tier; omitted, it is derived from the workspace's tier bands

reason.description: one line on why — shows on the record and in the score trail

scores.description: WRITE scores from your own scorer (up to 500). Needs `scorer`, and a workspace that scores for itself.

tools.name: set_icp
tools.description: Write (or replace) this workspace's ICP as markdown (body_md): who the ideal customer is, plus the scoring rules (a base, persona weights, firmographic weights, observed-signal boosts/cuts, and hard disqualifiers). The written ICP is replaced and versioned. The SCORING MODEL that score, get_context and the reports use is built from it only when the workspace has no model yet (a fresh workspace: whoami's setup says whether an ICP is set). When a model already exists it is KEPT as is, so the outcome-trained weights survive a text edit; the result says which happened. Read the current ICP first with query { scope: { foundation: 'icp' } } and keep what is still true. Authoring guide + required sections: the onboard skill's icp-authoring reference.

body_md.description: the full ICP as markdown — the buyer definition + the scoring rules (see the icp-authoring reference for the required sections)

tools.name: webhooks
tools.description: Push events to the user's own stack (n8n, Make, Clay, their agent's endpoint). Each record event carries the account, its people, the deal and the evidence behind it (source, confidence), so the receiver acts without calling back. Actions: `events` lists what can be subscribed to; `list`; `create` (url + events; returns the signing secret ONCE — tell the user to store it); `update` (name/url/events/active, or rotate_secret); `delete`; `test` sends one webhook.test now against a real account; `deliveries` shows recent sends and failures. Deliveries are signed: X-Nous-Signature = sha256 HMAC of the raw body with the secret.

id.description: The webhook id, for update, delete, test and deliveries.

events.description: Event types, e.g. conversation.call_ended, conversation.reply_received, deal.won, deal.lost, deal.stage_changed.

account_id.description: For test: the account to build the sample record from.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Get the full account record for a person or company — the durable FACTS we've learned about them (their atomic memory: budget, authority, pain, stack, plans), every attribute (claim) with its confidence and freshness, plus what they actually SAID and did, ranked by how much it tells you. Pass an email or entity UUID, and the intent you're working toward so the record is shaped for it.

id.description: Who to look up — an email, an entity UUID, or a name. A name may match several people; you'll get candidates to choose from.

intent.description: What you're about to do. Shapes how much of their history comes back: a meeting brief wants the conversation in detail, an email draft wants one hook. Defaults to account_review.

tools.name: deals
tools.description:
DEAL HEALTH and HOW LIKELY A DEAL IS TO CLOSE, with the reasons. Two ways to call it:
  • no `account` → the open deals most likely to close within `within_days` (default 30), ranked. Each carries its chance to close in that window, its overall chance to win, its deal health (score, band, what to watch) and the facts that moved its odds. Use for 'which deals are most likely to close in the next 30 days', 'what will close this month', 'what's closest to closing'.
  • `account` (email, domain, LinkedIn URL, entity UUID, or name) → that one deal: health with all four signals and the engagement read, its chance to close overall, within `within_days` and within 90 days, the stage-only baseline, and every fact pushing the odds up or down. Use for 'how likely is Acme to close', 'what's the deal health on Acme', 'will Acme close this month'.
The odds are the stage's base rate moved by what the graph recorded: open objections, competitors, stall, silence, threading, ICP fit, intent. 'unknown' within N days means this stage has no closed deals to judge timing on yet: say so, never call it 0%.
Until the workspace has enough won and lost deals to learn from, the odds come back as a RANK (ODDS TO CLOSE: 3rd most likely of 12 open deals) with what is helping and hurting, and NO percentage. Say it that way; never turn it into a percentage or call it a forecast, and don't explain model weights to the user.

account.description: One account to judge: email, domain, LinkedIn URL, entity UUID, or name. Omit to rank the open deals.

within_days.description: The window for 'likely to close within N days'. Default 30.

limit.description: How many ranked deals to return (max 25, default 10). Ignored with `account`.

tools.name: pages
tools.description:
The documents already written in this workspace — account briefs, account plans, reports (pipeline, win/loss, market read, forecast, team), meeting briefs, objection prep. The operator browses them in Pages.
  • `query` → the PASSAGES that match, best first, each with the section it came from. Use for 'what did we conclude about pricing', 'which report mentioned the Clay objection'.
  • no `query` → the list, newest first, filtered by `kind`, `account`, `series`, `cadence` or a date window. Use for 'last month's pipeline report', 'the brief on Acme', 'every win/loss read this quarter'.
CHECK HERE BEFORE WRITING A NEW REPORT OR BRIEF: build on the last one and say what changed. Open one with read_page. Cite a document by its ref (nous://doc/…) when you repeat what it found.

query.description: What you are looking for, in plain language. Omit to list.

account.description: Only documents about this account: email, domain, LinkedIn URL, entity UUID, or name.

cadence.description: Reports: the length of the window covered.

since.description: ISO date: documents covering or written on/after it.

until.description: ISO date: documents covering or written on/before it.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Read one document from `documents` — whole, one `section`, or the passages around a phrase (`find`, cheaper). Returns what the document cited (the calls and emails behind it, with quotes), the accounts it mentions, the documents it links to and that link to it, and its version history. When you repeat a finding, cite the SOURCE the document cited, not the document's summary of it.

section.description: Read only this section, by index.

find.description: A word or phrase: return the passages around each occurrence.

tools.name: save_page
tools.description:
File a FINISHED document into the workspace's Pages: an account brief, an account plan, a report (pipeline, win/loss, market read, forecast, team), a meeting brief or objection prep. It is saved on the account it is about, versioned (a new brief on the same account becomes the next version) and readable by the team and by agents. Call it ONCE, at the end, with the document you would otherwise have left in the chat or written to a file. Do NOT also write it to the repo: raw material (transcripts, emails) stays in git, the finished document lives in Pages.
HOW TO WRITE IT:
  • `markdown`: the document, split into sections on its `##` headings. A brief opens with an At a glance section of 4-6 bullets (a meeting brief opens with Purpose and objective instead); no headings or dividers inside a section. A report section opens with a thesis a reader could disagree with, never a label, and never as a negation followed by a correction.
  • CITE: mark each claim [1], [2] … and pass `sources` in that same order, each with the `ref` the tools printed (e.g. `source://fireflies/…`, `nous://account/…`) plus its quote and speaker when you have them. A marker with no matching source is dropped, so number against the list you pass.
  • A report passes `period` for the window it covers (it files under Weekly / Monthly / Quarterly) and `generated_from` with real product names ("HubSpot", "Fireflies").
After it returns, give the operator ONE line with the finding and the page link. Don't paste the document.

account.description: The account or person it is about: email, domain, LinkedIn URL, entity UUID, or name. Required for everything but a report across the book.

title.description: A report's name, as it would be called in an inbox ("Revenue Pipeline Report — Acme"). A meeting brief: the meeting's own title ("Acme x OpenNous"). A brief or plan is named by its account.

headline.description: One line: the finding, or where the account stands.

markdown.description: The document itself, sections on `##` headings, citations as [1], [2].

detail.description: What the source is: 'Pricing review call with Odile'.

sources.description: The evidence, in the order the [n] markers number it.

period.description: Reports: the window covered, ISO dates.

generated_from.description: Reports: the tools behind the data, as product names.

skill.description: The skill that produced it, e.g. 'brief', 'revenue-report'. Files a report into its series.

tools.name: record
tools.description: Record what happened or what you learned about a person or company. You never overwrite anything — you observe, and Nous derives the updated facts. Use kind:'event' for an interaction (property like 'interaction.email_sent', 'interaction.call_held', 'interaction.email_reply') and kind:'state' for a fact (property like 'job_title', 'deal.proposal_amount'). Examples — sent an email: {kind:'event',property:'interaction.email_sent',value:{description:'intro email'}}; learned their title changed: {kind:'state',property:'job_title',value:'VP of Engineering'}; a fact ended (they left): {kind:'state',property:'job_title',value:null}. For a piece of INTEL about the contact — a preference, an objection, a competitor they mentioned, a general note — use property:'intel' with a category: {kind:'state',property:'intel',value:{category:'objection',content:'skeptical about market demand',label:'Market demand skepticism'}} (category ∈ status_quo | goal | pain | objection | authority | budget | timeline | buying_signal | preference | competitor | discovery | relationship | adoption | proficiency | seasonality | staff_change | firmographic | performance | expansion_signal | risk_signal | tech_stack | blocker | requirement | general — use the MOST specific one; 'general' is a last resort, and it's 'timeline', never 'timing'. firmographic = the standing shape of the business (locations, headcount, volume they do, inventory, the segment they serve); performance = a dated result in THEIR business (a record month, a slump, leads or sales up or down, a target hit or missed); expansion_signal = an EXISTING customer asking for, considering or declining MORE of what we sell — set stance:'asked'|'considering'|'declined' and product:'<family name>', and never omit stance (a decline read as an ask sends a rep to pitch what was just refused); risk_signal = an EXISTING customer saying the relationship is in question — set severity:'stated_churn'|'at_risk'|'friction'. tech_stack = a tool they use and any fact about it, filed on the company, set tool:'<name>'; blocker = what stands between now and a signed deal, set status:'open'|'resolved'; requirement = a hard condition for buying. A prospect moving to close is buying_signal, not expansion_signal. Their feedback on OUR product is not intel about them: it is product feedback, not pain and not risk_signal). Insights about YOUR OWN business (product/positioning/market/buyer) go to record_insight, not here. HOW THIS OPERATOR WANTS THINGS — when they tell you outright, write it down so nobody has to say it twice. A preference is about shape: {kind:'state',property:'preference',value:{statement:'write shorter than feels finished',scope:'person',applies_to:'email_send'}}. A prohibition is stronger and gets its own property — {kind:'state',property:'constraint',value:{statement:'never send breakup emails',scope:'person'}} — because we stop generating those entirely rather than trying to remember not to. Use scope:'workspace' only when it is how the COMPANY works, not how this person likes things. CLOSING THE LOOP — when you RECOMMEND an action, write the recommendation down before it happens: {kind:'state',property:'decision.proposed',value:{decision_id:'<your id>',proposal:'send a follow-up naming the security objection',proposal_body:'<the exact draft>',rationale:'the security review is the real blocker at this stage', evidence_ids:['<claim/note id you reasoned from>'],action_type:'email_send',category:'outreach'}}. `proposal_body` is the draft itself — hashed and discarded, never stored, and the only way to tell later whether the human sent it as written or rewrote it first. Omit it and the decision reports as sent-verbatim whatever happened. Keep `proposal` (WHAT you are doing) apart from `rationale` (WHY you think it works), and list the facts you actually reasoned from in `evidence_ids` — that is what lets Nous learn which KINDS of evidence are worth acting on, not just which actions worked. When the human answers, record the verdict: property 'decision.accepted' | 'decision.edited' | 'decision.rejected' with the same decision_id. PASS drafted_body AND sent_body whenever you can see the final text — a rewrite in the conversation, a pasted-back version, a revision you produced on request. Without them the verdict is stored UNVERIFIED and counts toward nothing, so reporting 'edited' with no text is the same as saying nothing. On the verdict, say what the correction MEANT — you are the only one who heard it: {interpretation:'cut the pricing paragraph', correction_kind:'rule'|'structure'|'claim'|'constraint'|'none', correction_scope:'once'|'person'|'workspace'|'product'}. 'none' and 'once' are correct most of the time; a typo or a detail only they knew teaches nothing, and recording it crowds out the real signal. Ask 'just this one, or always?' only when you genuinely cannot tell. Then pass that same decision_id on the interaction observation when the action fires. That is what turns advice into learnable data — without it a send is an orphan nobody can grade.

focus.description: Email address, LinkedIn URL, domain, or entity UUID — a precise identifier, never a bare name

kind.description: event = an interaction; state = a fact

value.description: the event detail or the fact value; null = the fact ended

source.description: where this came from — provider slug, e.g. 'fireflies', 'gmail' (default: agent)

method.description: api | webhook | extraction | inference | user_input (default: api)

observed_at.description: ISO timestamp of WHEN this happened/was true. REQUIRED when importing history — otherwise it's stamped now.

external_id.description: idempotency key, unique per (source). Re-recording the same one is a no-op. One raw item → many observations → give each a distinct id, e.g. '<itemId>:<property>'.

source_ref.description: pointer to the raw this came from, e.g. 'git://<repo>/raw/fireflies/2026-03-14-9182.md'. Keeps provenance without storing raw in Nous.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the raw file, so a later fetch can be verified untampered. Set when raw lives in git (not sent here).

decision_id.description: the recommendation this action came from. Stamp it on the interaction observation you record when the action fires (an email send, a LinkedIn message) and Nous attributes whatever comes back — reply, meeting, bounce, silence — to that decision.

observations.description: One or more observations to record

tools.name: record_insight
tools.description: Record what a call or email taught us about OUR OWN business — our product, positioning, market, or buyer. This is the MIRROR of record: record captures facts about the CONTACT; this captures what we learned about US. Workspace-level — there is no focus (it's not about one account). category is one of product | positioning | market | buyer. Include the verbatim quote and who said it whenever you can. These feed the Insights page and its theme clustering. Send all insights from one source in a single call. Do NOT put contact facts here — use record.

content.description: the insight in one clear sentence, stated from OUR perspective

quote.description: the verbatim thing they said that supports it

speaker.description: who said it — a name or a role

insights.description: one or more insights extracted from the same call/email

source_label.description: where these came from, e.g. 'Acme discovery call'

tools.name: record_closed_deals
tools.description: Train this workspace's ICP on REAL closed deals. Pass the won and lost deals (each a bare domain, or an object {domain, amount, currency, closed_at}). The engine enriches each domain, links the contacts you already have there, resolves their open ICP predictions with the real outcome, runs contrastive lift (the signals that separate wins from losses), and re-scores every open account against the upgraded model. Use it in onboarding once the backfill has landed the closed cohorts (pull them with query scope.property:'stage' — accounts at 'closed_won' and 'closed_lost'), and whenever new deals close. Needs at least one deal; both sides (some won AND some lost) make the lift trustworthy — one side alone is directional only. The ICP is the one company model, so this is an admin/founder action.

amount.description: Deal value in major units (48000, not 4800000).

currency.description: ISO code or symbol. Defaults to the workspace currency.

closed_at.description: When it actually closed, ISO date. Drives every cycle-time measurement, so pass the real date rather than today's.

won.description: Closed-WON deals — bare domains or {domain, amount, currency, closed_at}. Pull from accounts at stage 'closed_won'.

lost.description: Closed-LOST deals — same shape. Pull from accounts at stage 'closed_lost'.
